analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md; the changes are documentation only, so no executable code paths changed. The changed ranges visible to me are the 'Last updated' date bump, a new paragraph at head lines 3528-3536, and edits to the cluster runtime facts section at about head lines 5230+ (outside the supplied excerpts, beyond line 3998).

Head 3528-3536 documents that the cluster service writes its heartbeat to the file named by DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE, and that the supervisor's liveness guard accepts only a beat carrying the service's own PID. It also says ClusterService.partEnvironment gives the coordinator-paired part a separate file (part-health.json), so the part cannot overwrite the service heartbeat. This is a described availability and integrity control on a local supervision file. It does not touch the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), or the prefix-cache (T-041) or add-on hold (TB-012) boundaries. I could not verify the implementation, such as file permissions or PID validation, because no source was supplied. This is a documentation claim, not an observed regression.

The remaining excerpt text is pre-existing and unchanged: Flint tool constraints, tensor-parallel probes, and link and share probe history files. These files are described as owner-only under ~/.darkbloom/cluster, consistent with the existing local-state posture.

The cluster runtime facts edit (the signed release registers digests via cluster_runtime, and guided setup recomputes them) is only partially visible and its patch excerpt is truncated. That text touches admission approval digests, a trust-relevant area. The implementation, the release lane and the coordinator-side matching are outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should check that the claimed computation matches the code if source files are in other batches. No threat-model IDs are invalidated by the visible content.
